title: Medea
author: Euripides
openingText: NURSE. (The Nurse of Medea's Children enters.) If only Argo had never sped between the blue Clashing Rocks towards Kolchis-land, if only the pine had never fallen under an axe in Pelion's valleys, and no oars had filled the hands of those princely heroes sent by Pelias to seek the Golden Fleece!
about:
Jason has left Medea for the daughter of Kreon, ruler of Corinth. Medea helped him win the Golden Fleece and left her own home to follow him. Now she faces exile with their children. The play follows her response through confrontations with Kreon, Jason and Aigeus, while the women of Corinth listen, sympathise and challenge her.

The action repeatedly turns on speech: promises, excuses, oaths and requests for help. Medea's position as a foreign woman matters to her argument, but her suffering does not settle the question of what she may do in response. Listen for the point at which the Chorus's sympathy turns into opposition.

This modern edition follows the English source supplied with this collection, preserving its seven-chapter structure, mythic details and stage directions. The Chorus speaks collectively and sometimes in the singular. The Children's Guardian is an enslaved attendant, rather than a modern legal guardian. The oracle about the wine-skin is deliberately riddling. Ancient measures such as plethra are retained rather than silently converted. Violent events, including violence against children, are part of the tragedy.

whyItMatters.title: Arguments under pressure
whyItMatters.body: Each encounter gives Medea a different audience. Notice how she changes her appeal and what each person agrees to.

whyItMatters.title: The costs of belonging
whyItMatters.body: Marriage, citizenship, exile and hospitality shape the characters' choices. The same promise can offer safety to one person and create danger for another.

whyItMatters.title: A divided will
whyItMatters.body: Medea's speeches move between affection, anger and calculation. Follow those changes without assuming that a single motive explains everything.

angleCards.title: Listen to the promises
angleCards.text: Track who swears an oath, who breaks one, and who asks for more than a spoken assurance.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to trace promises and oaths in Medea and see how they shape each character's choices.

angleCards.title: Compare Medea and Jason
angleCards.text: Set their accounts of the past and of the new marriage beside each other. Which facts do they agree on, and where do their judgments diverge?
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to compare Medea's and Jason's arguments without automatically accepting either speaker's account.

angleCards.title: Follow the Chorus
angleCards.text: Watch when the women offer support, when they object, and what they can or cannot prevent.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to follow the Chorus's changing response to Medea and its role in the tragedy.

cast.name: Medea
cast.description: A woman from Kolchis who helped Jason obtain the Golden Fleece. She is threatened with exile from Corinth.

cast.name: Jason
cast.description: Medea's husband and the father of their children. He defends his new marriage as a benefit to the family.

cast.name: Kreon
cast.description: Father of Jason's new bride. He fears Medea and orders her to leave.

cast.name: Aigeus
cast.description: He arrives after consulting an oracle about his childlessness. Medea asks him for refuge.

cast.name: The Nurse and the Children's Guardian
cast.description: They care for the children and speak of their concern for Medea and the household.

cast.name: The Chorus
cast.description: They hear Medea's arguments and respond to what unfolds outside the house.
